_doc: The outside of the ship while it lies in the space dock (openspec/changes/deck-pipeline, design section 13b; read by sc-core::exterior::ExteriorData). Directions are ship coordinates: +x port, +y up, +z the bow; any length. Colours are sRGB 0-1. The sky program (crates/sc-render/shaders/sky.glsl) draws the stars, the sun and the planet from them; deckc builds the dock's girders from `dock` into the deck file, and the client draws the bow camera's view onto every viewscreen from `viewscreen`.

planet._doc: A planet below the ship to port, filling a good part of the port windows: its centre's direction and the angle its disc spans from the centre to the limb.

stars._doc: density: the share of grid cells that hold a star (three grids of 3 sizes); brightness: the brightest star's value.

dock._doc: A frame of steel girders round the hull (the Tern is 84 m long, 24.4 m across and 13.8 m high): ring frames every ring_spacing_m along z, longitudinal girders at the corners and mid sides, cross braces on the sides, and a work light at each ring's inner corners. Built by deckc into compartments of the deck `outside`, each within one bay so its vertices stay in the deck vertex's +/-32 m.

beacons._doc: The navigation beacons on stations and relays outside (openspec/changes/patrol-mission design 3): each blinks once a period, lit for on_s of it, and is drawn at least min_radius_deg in angular radius however far off it is (about 3 pixels across at 70 degrees on 720 lines), so the relay's light shows from 18 km.

viewscreen._doc: The bow camera: where it sits (just ahead of the hull's bow), the way it looks (ahead, turned a little to port and down so the planet's limb is in the corner), its vertical field of view and the target it renders into each frame, pixels.

chase._doc: The chase camera (openspec/changes/chase-camera design 1): CHASE is a toggle, and with it on any viewscreen camera (TARGET, FWD, PORT, AFT, STBD) is seen from behind the Tern: distance_m back along the line the camera looks (TARGET: from the target through the ship's centre), raised so the ship's centre sits ship_low of the half height below the middle of the picture and in the middle across, looking the camera's way (TARGET: at the target). fov_across_deg is its field of view across the feed at zoom 1.
chase._follow: openspec/changes/chase-orbit design 3-5: follow_tau_s is the time constant of the critically damped lag with which the chase camera follows the ship's turn in the system frame (turning at a steady rate it settles follow_tau_s of the turn behind: 7.2 degrees at the Tern's 18 degrees a second); blend_s how long a change of camera, CHASE or ORBIT eases from the old picture to the new. orbit: the chase camera turned round the ship by hand, distance_m the nearest and farthest from the ship's centre, pitch_limit_deg the look line's tilt above or below the ship, drag_deg_across the heading a drag across the whole viewscreen turns (half that of elevation down it), wheel_step the distance's factor a wheel notch, smooth_tau_s the time constant the orbit drawn follows the hand's with, send_hz the most times a second the captain's orbit is sent to the main viewscreen while it changes.
